slot.brief: Three complexes given with ligands/metal ions; determine hybridisation (d2sp3 vs sp3d2), spin state and magnetic moment — must first assign metal oxidation states, then apply VBT at higher difficulty.

stem: Let I = $[\text{Co}(en)_3]^{3+}$, II = $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$ and III = $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$. Which row gives the hybridisation, spin state, number of unpaired electrons $n$ and spin-only magnetic moment for I, II and III? Use $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{BM}$.

verdicts.working: I: Co³⁺ is d⁶; en gives low-spin d²sp³, n=0. II: Fe³⁺ is d⁵; F⁻ gives high-spin sp³d², n=5, μ=√35≈5.92 BM. III: Mn³⁺ is d⁴; CN⁻ gives low-spin d²sp³, n=2, μ=√8≈2.83 BM. These match option A.

working:
I: $\text{Co}^{3+}:d^6$; strong-field $en$ gives low spin, $d^2sp^3$, $n=0$, $\mu=0$. 
II: $\text{Fe}^{3+}:d^5$; weak-field $\text{F}^-$ gives high spin, $sp^3d^2$, $n=5$, $\mu=\sqrt{35}=5.92\ \text{BM}$. 
III: $\text{Mn}^{3+}:d^4$; strong-field $\text{CN}^-$ gives low spin, $d^2sp^3$, $n=2$, $\mu=\sqrt{8}=2.83\ \text{BM}$.

Independent check: I: Co³⁺ is d⁶; en gives low-spin d²sp³, n=0. II: Fe³⁺ is d⁵; F⁻ gives high-spin sp³d², n=5, μ=√35≈5.92 BM. III: Mn³⁺ is d⁴; CN⁻ gives low-spin d²sp³, n=2, μ=√8≈2.83 BM. These match option A.
solution:
For octahedral complexes, $en$ and $CN^-$ cause pairing, while $F^-$ gives high spin. Thus Co$^{3+}$ ($d^6$): $d^2sp^3$, $n=0$; Fe$^{3+}$ ($d^5$): $sp^3d^2$, $n=5$; Mn$^{3+}$ ($d^4$): $d^2sp^3$, $n=2$.
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$$
The moments are $0$, $\sqrt{35}=5.92$ BM and $\sqrt{8}=2.83$ BM, respectively; these match (B).
